# Amos Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 336r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/AMO_007_page_001.jpg

---

**1** This is what the Lord GOD showed me: behold, he was forming locusts when the latter growth was just beginning to sprout, and behold, it was the latter growth after the king's mowings. **2** When they had finished eating the vegetation of the land, I said, "O Lord GOD, please forgive! How can Jacob stand? He is so small!" **3** The LORD relented concerning this: "It shall not be," said the LORD.

**7** This is what he showed me: behold, the Lord was standing beside a wall built with a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand. **8** And the LORD said to me, "Amos, what do you see?" And I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Behold, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel; I will never again pass by them."

**10** Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words."

**14** Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I was no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but I was a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs. **15** But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'"

**17** Therefore thus says the LORD: "'Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be divided up with a measuring line; you yourself shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall surely go into exile away from its land.'"

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"I was no prophet" (v.14):** Amos's most famous self-description. He is not a professional religious figure or member of a prophetic guild. He is a rancher and farmer whom YHWH pulled from behind the flock and sent to prophesy. This is Amos's authority claim: he didn't choose this career — God drafted him.

**The Amaziah confrontation (vv.10-17):** The priest of Bethel tries to silence the prophet by reporting him to the king. It's the classic conflict between institutional religion and prophetic critique — and it still happens everywhere.

*— PNEUMA*
